title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Remonstrants themselves place preaching under common providence — we grant that, adding special mercy for the elect and permission of contrary effect for the rest
pass_a_gloss: The Remonstrants themselves understand, when it is for their purpose, that the preaching of the Gospel does not flow from some absolute decree of saving or damning all and singular unto whom it is preached, but from a certain more common reason of providence, which they call the wise, merciful, and just government of Christ, Collat. Hagiens. pag. 95. Let them therefore suffer us also to subscribe unto their sentence, this being added: that Evangelical preaching flows from the decree of predestination as to those in whom God decreed of his special mercy by that organ to work penitence, faith, and salvation infallibly; but that Evangelical preaching flows from a certain more common reason of providence as to those in whom God decreed to permit that by their fault it should obtain an effect plainly contrary; yet so that as to these latter we by no means grant that it flows from the decree of reprobation, or is subordinated as a medium unto their damnation by the primary intention of God.
pass_b_english: The Remonstrants themselves, when it suits them, take Gospel preaching not to flow from some absolute decree to save or damn every hearer, but from a more common providence — what they call Christ's wise, merciful, and just government (Collat. Hagiens. p. 95). Let them then let us subscribe that view, with this added: preaching flows from the predestination decree for those in whom God decreed of special mercy to work penitence, faith, and salvation infallibly through that instrument; and it flows from a more common providence for those in whom he decreed to permit that by their fault it should take a plainly contrary effect — yet we never grant that for these latter it flows from the reprobation decree, or is subordinated as a medium to their damnation by God's primary intention.
source_text: Ipsi Remonstrantes intelligunt, quando ex re ipsorum est, praedicationem Evangelii non manare ex absoluto aliquo decreto salvandi aut damnandi omnes et singulos quibus praedicatur, sed ex communiori quadam ratione providentiae, quam illi vocant sapientem, misericordem, et justam Christi gubernationem, Collat. Hagiens. pag. 95. Patiantur igitur et nos illorum sententiae subscribere, hoc addito, Evangelicam praedicationem ex decreto praedestinationis manare quoad illos, in quibus Deus decrevit ex speciali sua misericordia per illud organon poenitentiam, fidem, et salutem infallibiliter operari; Evangelicam autem praedicationem ex communiori quadam providentiae ratione manare quoad illos, in quibus Deus decrevit permittere ut illorum vitio effectum sortiatur plane contrarium; ita tamen ut quoad hosce posteriores ex decreto reprobationis fluere, aut tanquam medium damnationi eorundem primaria Dei intentione subordinatum esse, nullo modo concedamus.
